question: What is the most common developmental complication in bacterial meningitis in the pediatric age?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "damage to cochlea" -> "hearing loss" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of brain tissue" -> "seizure activity" -> "residual epilepsy" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of brain tissue" -> "cognitive impairment" -> "mental retardation" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow" -> "ventricular enlargement" -> "hydrocephalus" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Bacterial meningitis" -> "inflammation of optic nerve" -> "possible visual defects" -> 50%
analysis: Hearing loss is the most common developmental complication following bacterial meningitis in children. This is due to the potential damage to the cochlea and auditory pathways caused by the infection and inflammation. While other complications like residual epilepsy, mental retardation, hydrocephalus, and visual defects can occur, hearing loss is the most frequently observed long-term sequela.
